content.text:
Sync watchers now fire in the order they were registered, whether they watch a `ref` or a `computed`. The unit tests in reactivity, runtime-core, runtime-dom and server-renderer pass (1723 passed, 4 skipped). The e2e suites failed in the full run; my reading is that they need a browser that isn't set up here. I didn't add a regression test for this.

**Cause:** sync watchers had a special "no batching" mode, so they ran right away during notification. Notification walks a value's subscribers from newest to oldest, which is why they came out last-in-first-out.

**Fix (2 files):**
- **`packages/reactivity/src/effect.ts`**: I removed the "no batching" flag and its shortcut in `notify()`. Sync watchers now go through the normal batch, which runs subscribers oldest first. I also changed `endBatch()` to lower the batch depth before running the queued effects rather than after. Without that, a write made inside a sync watcher would be held back, and the existing test "sync watcher should not be batched" failed.
- **`packages/runtime-core/src/apiWatch.ts`**: removed the line that set that flag on sync watchers.

**Check:** I registered five sync watchers on a `ref` and five on a `computed` of it, alternating. The output was `r0, c0, c1, c2, c3, c4, r1, r2, r3, r4`. Each group runs in its own registration order. All the `computed` watchers run together at the point where the computed first subscribed to the ref, which was when the first one (`c0`) was created.
